lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: # ADR Format

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: ADRs live in `docs/adr/` and use sequential numbering: `0001-slug.md`, `0002-slug.md`, etc.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: Create the `docs/adr/` directory lazily — only when the first ADR is needed.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: ## Template

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: ```md

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: # {Short title of the decision}

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: {1-3 sentences: what's the context, what did we decide, and why.}

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: That's it. An ADR can be a single paragraph. The value is in recording *that* a decision was made and *why* — not in filling out sections.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: ## Optional sections

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: Only include these when they add genuine value. Most ADRs won't need them.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - **Status** frontmatter (`proposed | accepted | deprecated | superseded by ADR-NNNN`) — useful when decisions are revisited

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - **Considered Options** — only when the rejected alternatives are worth remembering

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - **Consequences** — only when non-obvious downstream effects need to be called out

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: ## Numbering

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: Scan `docs/adr/` for the highest existing number and increment by one.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: ## When to offer an ADR

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: All three of these must be true:

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: 1. **Hard to reverse** — the cost of changing your mind later is meaningful

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: 2. **Surprising without context** — a future reader will look at the code and wonder "why on earth did they do it this way?"

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: 3. **The result of a real trade-off** — there were genuine alternatives and you picked one for specific reasons

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: If a decision is easy to reverse, skip it — you'll just reverse it. If it's not surprising, nobody will wonder why. If there was no real alternative, there's nothing to record beyond "we did the obvious thing."

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: ### What qualifies

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - **Architectural shape.** "We're using a monorepo." "The write model is event-sourced, the read model is projected into Postgres."

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - **Integration patterns between contexts.** "Ordering and Billing communicate via domain events, not synchronous HTTP."

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - **Technology choices that carry lock-in.** Database, message bus, auth provider, deployment target. Not every library — just the ones that would take a quarter to swap out.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - **Boundary and scope decisions.** "Customer data is owned by the Customer context; other contexts reference it by ID only." The explicit no-s are as valuable as the yes-s.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - **Deliberate deviations from the obvious path.** "We're using manual SQL instead of an ORM because X." Anything where a reasonable reader would assume the opposite. These stop the next engineer from "fixing" something that was deliberate.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - **Constraints not visible in the code.** "We can't use AWS because of compliance requirements." "Response times must be under 200ms because of the partner API contract."

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - **Rejected alternatives when the rejection is non-obvious.** If you considered GraphQL and picked REST for subtle reasons, record it — otherwise someone will suggest GraphQL again in six months.
